Fact.Description: Schedule 1-A line 3 (MAGI): line 1 (1040 line 11b, AGI) plus line 2e (§911/931/933 exclusions). Direct File supports none of those exclusions, so line 2e is 0 and MAGI = AGI. §151(d)(5)(C)(iii)(II).

§224(d)(1): "cash tips received by an individual in an occupation which customarily and regularly received tips on or before December 31, 2024, as provided by the Secretary." Asked when a W-2 has box 12 code TP (the occupation code is in box 14b). Placeholder false: no deduction unless confirmed. The screen text also excludes mandatory amounts: 2026 draft Form 1040 instructions, p.102: "Qualified tips do not include service charges, automatic gratuities, or any other mandatory amounts automatically added to a customer's bill by the vendor or the establishment, unless the customer is expressly provided an option to disregard or modify such charges, gratuities, and amounts without consequence." (§224(d)(2)(A): "paid voluntarily without any consequence in the event of nonpayment").
§224(d)(2)(B): tips from a specified service trade or business (§199A(d)(2)) are not qualified; an employee is treated as in an SSTB if the employer is. Placeholder false.
§224(c): self-employed tips count only up to net income of the trade or business (Schedule 1-A line 6). Not supported. Asked when the return has a Schedule C business. Placeholder false.

Fact.Name: §224 SSTB interim rule (draft Form 1040 instructions p.102)
Fact.Description: #57. Draft Form 1040 instructions (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040gi--dft.pdf), Schedule 1-A Part II, p.102: "Until the issuance of final regulations determining whether a trade or business is an SSTB for purposes of this deduction, and for taxable years beginning before the date the final regulations are published, the IRS will treat employees and self-employed individuals as having received tips in the course of a trade or business that is not an SSTB if the employee is in an occupation that customarily and regularly received tips on or before December 31, 2024." (transition relief: Notice 2025-69). IRC §224(d)(2)(B) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/224). True while no final SSTB regulations for §224 have been published; set to false when they are, which restores the SSTB question and stop below.

Fact.Name: Ask the SSTB question
Fact.Description: #57. Asked only when code TP tips are present, the filer confirmed a listed tipped occupation (otherwise line 5 is $0 and the SSTB answer cannot change the return), and the p.102 interim rule no longer applies. While it applies, a confirmed listed occupation is treated as not from an SSTB.

Fact.Name: Knockout: tips from a specified service trade or business
Fact.Description: §224(d)(2)(B): tips from an SSTB (§199A(d)(2)) are not qualified tips. #57: under the p.102 interim rule a filer in a confirmed listed tipped occupation is treated as not in an SSTB, so this stop fires only when the interim rule no longer applies (/flowShowTipsSstbQuestion) and the filer answers that the employer is an SSTB. Wired into /flowIsKnockedOut in flow.xml.

Fact.Name: Knockout: tips received in the filer's own trade or business

Fact.Description: Line 5: qualified employee tips, W-2 box 12 code TP (lines 4a-4e column (iii)). Zero unless the occupation is confirmed and the filer is not MFS (§224(f)). Per-W-2 valid SSN is applied in formW2s. #202: rounded to whole dollars once the column (iii) amounts are added. Instructions for Form 1040 (2025), p. 23, Rounding Off to Whole Dollars: "If you have to add two or more amounts to figure the amount to enter on a line, include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total." 26 U.S.C. 6102(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/6102) rounds half up.

Line 9: "Enter the smaller of the amount on line 8 or $25,000" (line 8 = line 5 + line 7; line 7 is 0 because self-employed tips are knocked out). §224(b)(1): "shall not exceed $25,000." Per return, not per spouse.
Line 11: "Enter $150,000 ($300,000 if married filing jointly)". §224(b)(2)(A).
Line 12: line 10 (= line 3 MAGI) minus line 11, not below zero.

Line 13: "Divide line 12 by $1,000. If the resulting number isn't a whole number, decrease the result to the next lower whole number." §224(b)(2)(A) "$100 for each $1,000 by which" MAGI exceeds the threshold has no "or fraction thereof", so a partial $1,000 is ignored. StepwiseMultiply = floor(x / 1000) x 1.
Line 14: "Multiply line 13 by $100".
Line 15: "Qualified tips deduction. Subtract line 14 from line 9. If zero or less, enter -0-."
Schedule 1-A line 27, qualified overtime compensation deduction (Part III). Placeholder for #52.
Schedule 1-A line 36, qualified passenger vehicle loan interest deduction (Part IV). #53: computed in carLoanInterest.xml.
"$6,000 for each qualified individual" — §151(d)(5)(C)(i). Not inflation-indexed.
Line 38: "Enter $75,000 ($150,000 if married filing jointly)". §151(d)(5)(C)(iii)(I).
Line 39: line 37 (= line 3) minus line 38, not below zero.

Line 40: line 39 x 6%. 2026 draft Schedule 1-A (Created 6/16/26), https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040s1a--dft.pdf, line 40: "Multiply line 39 by 6% (0.06)". The statute ("6 percent of so much of ... MAGI as exceeds") has no $1,000 increments, unlike line 34 for car loan interest. #202: the line itself is rounded to whole dollars as it is computed, so line 41 ("Subtract line 40 from $6,000") and lines 43, 44 and Form 1040 line 13a/14 come out whole. 26 U.S.C. 6102(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/6102): "the fractional part of a dollar shall be disregarded unless it amounts to one-half dollar or more, in which case the amount ... shall be increased by $1"; 26 CFR 301.6102-1(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/26/301.6102-1) rounds half up. Instructions for Form 1040 (2025), p. 23, Rounding Off to Whole Dollars: "If you do round to whole dollars, you must round all amounts."
Line 41: $6,000 minus line 40; if zero or less, -0-. "(but not below zero)".
§151(d)(5)(C)(v): a married individual (§7703) qualifies only on a joint return. MFS gets 0. HOH filers are treated as unmarried under §7703(b); Single/QSS are unmarried.
Line 42a test: valid SSN (§151(d)(5)(C)(iv), §24(h)(7)) and age 65 by year end (born before January 2, 1962; age65OrOlder uses the day-before-birthday rule).
Line 42b test: MFJ only, spouse valid SSN and age 65 by year end.
Line 43: enhanced deduction for seniors, lines 42a + 42b.
Line 44: "Add lines 15, 27, 36, and 43. Enter here and on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 13a". Below the line: allowed with the standard deduction or itemizing.
